projects.name: Conversion-by-Source Attribution (ATC → Purchase)
projects.description: Extend the ATC-source attribution (live 2026-06-08, ThemeSmith atc-tracking.js -> GA4 -> DataOps raw_ga4_atc -> atc-source.html) from a top-of-funnel 'where do adds originate' view into a full-funnel 'which source converts' view. Today the atc_source signal rides only on the add_to_cart event, so we can see adds by source (pdp / collection-quickadd / upcart-upsell / cart / collection / other) but NOT which source actually drives purchases, revenue, or contribution margin. RECOMMENDED PATH (B): ThemeSmith stamps the source as a Shopify cart line-item property (_atc_source) at add-to-cart time; it persists through checkout natively and lands on the order line item; DataOps extends ingest_shopify.py to pull line-item customAttributes into raw_line_items as a first-class column; conversion-by-source becomes a clean SQL join against units sold / revenue / True Gross / margin that the pipeline already computes. This lands the source signal where the money is and joins to existing profit metrics, unlike the GA4-native alternative (Path A: item_list_name through to purchase) which is lossy and siloed in GA4 with no margin join. Live-cart instrumentation requires Justin sign-off before shipping.

incidents.rootCause: AgentSmith dispatched the cleanup with insufficient safety thinking. CatalogSmith's phantom signal (duplicate-SKU + non-active-status) inverts reality at Teeccino, where status=archived/draft/unlisted is the canonical hidden-but-active state for cart-addable products. Single safety guard (skip status=active) caught 48/83 entries; the remaining 35 included ~19 active products. Free Java Packet 7976160755960 — explicitly named in Shopkeeper CLAUDE.md as the FOTM Free Packet — got renamed despite being a hard-rule ID, because the hard-rule was in markdown text, not in a machine-readable refuse-list.
